documentation.supports: Enhanced spell check sends editable text to Google when enabled.
User preferences may override the spellcheck content attribute; its reflected property is not the complete effective checking state.
browser.newContext creates isolated non-persistent, incognito-like contexts.

sourceFindings: The reviewed client uploads a request body through a browser-process URL-loader factory.
Availability requires enabled spelling preferences and rejects off-the-record contexts.
This function takes a BrowserContext and text; this review has not established the complete upstream page-policy path.

nativeSuccessControl.result: Synthetic marker received by owned local substitute for remote service.

runtimeMitigation.result: Selected persistent profile: twenty DOM checks preserve disabled spelling and ordinary XML data, no marker in six seconds; restoring the actual native IDL setter transmits the marker.
unresolved: Proof of caller ownership and native correspondence

implications: Ordinary editable text is a browser-service effect boundary; script/resource mediation is insufficient evidence for it.
Incognito-like contexts cannot calibrate a service explicitly disabled off the record.
An HTML spellcheck=false attribute is not an unconditional browser-security boundary under the standard user-preference override.
Persistent full-browser tests reduce one environment gap; they do not establish remote-service behavior or disable user-enabled services.
